id: Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctuary 4:17
q_practical: Why did some ancient sacrifices go ahead even though many people hadn't purified themselves first?
q_conceptual: Is it ever allowed to push a religious calendar around just to work around a purity problem?

id: Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctuary 4:18
q_practical: Did a king ever get forgiven for making a calendar mistake in a religious ritual?
q_conceptual: Can sincere prayer make up for a procedural error in how a festival was scheduled?

id: Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctuary 4:2
q_practical: What happened to a priest caught serving while unclean instead of being tried in court?
q_conceptual: Why would a religious community bypass its own courts to punish an offense on the spot?

id: Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctuary 9:12
q_practical: If someone breaks two rules at once doing the same forbidden act, do they get punished twice?
q_conceptual: How does the law handle a single act that violates multiple separate prohibitions?

q_practical: How late in the month can I still say a blessing over the new moon if I missed the first night?
q_conceptual: Why would a prayer only be tied to a particular phase of the moon?

q_practical: My first two babies died shortly after being circumcised — should I still circumcise my third son on schedule?
q_conceptual: Why would saving a life take priority over performing a religious ritual on time?

q_practical: How long can I wait before circumcising a servant who doesn't want it done?
q_conceptual: What options does a household have when someone under its authority refuses a required ritual?

q_practical: If a terminally ill person's animal kills someone, does the animal still get put down?
q_conceptual: Why would an owner's own legal status affect whether their animal is punished?

q_practical: If a pregnant animal is condemned to death for killing someone, does its unborn baby share the same fate?
q_conceptual: Why would an unborn animal inherit the legal status of the crime committed by its mother?

q_practical: A cow that killed someone later had a calf — is the calf allowed to be used normally?
q_conceptual: Why would the timing of a birth relative to a legal sentence change whether the offspring is affected?

q_practical: How small a piece of contaminated fabric is enough to make an entire building unclean?
q_conceptual: Why would the law borrow its minimum measurements from an unrelated category like human remains?

q_practical: If a house is officially condemned as contaminated, does just touching the outside wall count as contact?
q_conceptual: Why would a final ruling of contamination expand the reach of the impurity beyond what applied before?

id: Mishneh Torah, Defilement by a Corpse 8:5
q_practical: I found an unmarked grave on my land — can I move the body somewhere else?
q_conceptual: Why would it matter whether people already knew a grave was there before deciding if you can relocate it?

id: Mishneh Torah, Defilement by a Corpse 8:6
q_practical: A grave near my property is a public hazard — can it be dug up and moved?
q_conceptual: Why would removing a grave for public safety still leave the ground it came from off-limits?

q_practical: Does spilling fruit juice on food make it more likely to catch contamination, the way water would?
q_conceptual: Why would only a specific short list of liquids trigger this kind of contamination risk?

q_practical: I stored salted olives in a sealed jar without a drainage hole — does the liquid that builds up make them susceptible to contamination?
q_conceptual: Why would whether you intended liquid to touch the food determine whether contamination can take hold?

q_practical: Can I use a leather strap to join a wool item and a linen item together, or does that still count as mixing them?
q_conceptual: Why would tying two fabrics together with a completely different third material still count as combining them?

q_practical: If a vine of mine grows over a neighbor's grain crop, does his crop become unusable?
q_conceptual: Why can someone only cause their own property to become forbidden, not someone else's?

q_practical: Can the messenger who delivered my divorce papers and vouched for their validity later marry me himself?
q_conceptual: Why would someone be barred from marrying a person whose eligibility to remarry they personally certified?

q_practical: If the man I couldn't marry because of who vouched for me later becomes single again, can we marry then?
q_conceptual: Why would a restriction on marrying someone disappear once their other spouse is no longer in the picture?

q_practical: My husband was reported dead so I remarried his brother, but then my husband came back — what happens now?
q_conceptual: What happens legally when someone believed dead turns out to be alive after their spouse has already remarried?

q_practical: I remarried after hearing my husband died, but then found out he'd been alive the whole time — do I need to formally separate from my second husband?
q_conceptual: Why would a marriage that was never legally possible not require a formal divorce to undo?

q_practical: What exactly needs to be written down when a young girl formally rejects a marriage her family arranged for her?
q_conceptual: Why would a document recording someone's refusal of a marriage need witnesses and a physical exam to back it up?

q_practical: Can a man take his wife back after divorcing her because she cheated?
q_conceptual: Why would a spouse be legally barred from staying with a partner after infidelity, with only one exception?

q_practical: Can a woman who can't hear or speak get out of a marriage arranged for her as easily as a minor can?
q_conceptual: Why would the law deliberately withhold an easy exit from marriage from one group, even at a cost to them, for the sake of their marriage prospects?

q_practical: Does an older woman past childbearing years still have to wait several months before remarrying after a divorce?
q_conceptual: Why would a waiting period before remarriage apply even when the reason behind it obviously doesn't?

q_practical: A young girl's marriage was annulled by a court because it turned out to be invalid — does she still need to wait before remarrying?
q_conceptual: Why would a waiting-period rule not apply to situations the lawmakers never anticipated?

q_practical: Can a young girl call off a marriage her family arranged for her more than once?
q_conceptual: Why would a minor's right to reject a marriage arrangement have no limit on how many times she can use it?

q_practical: What does a young girl actually have to say to formally reject a marriage arranged for her?
q_conceptual: Why would simply stating a rejection in front of witnesses be enough to end the marriage, without any formal paperwork?

q_practical: What does the document look like when a young girl formally rejects her arranged marriage?
q_conceptual: Why does this rejection document deliberately avoid sounding like an official divorce certificate?

q_practical: Two witnesses disagree about whether my husband is dead — am I allowed to remarry?
q_conceptual: Why does contradictory testimony about a death block remarriage even when one witness seems credible?

q_practical: My husband's other wife says he's dead, but I don't believe her — does her claim affect whether I can remarry?
q_conceptual: Why can't one of a man's wives testify about his death on behalf of the other?

q_practical: I once falsely claimed my husband divorced me, and now I'm reporting he died — will anyone believe me?
q_conceptual: Why would someone's past dishonesty about their marriage affect how their later testimony is treated?

q_practical: Can a man's own confession that he killed someone be used to let that person's widow remarry?
q_conceptual: Why would a confession that could incriminate someone still count as valid evidence for someone else's benefit?

q_practical: Can I believe a stranger who casually mentions in conversation that someone died?
q_conceptual: Why does an offhand remark count as more trustworthy evidence than a statement made with an obvious motive?

q_practical: If someone only reveals the full story about a death after being pressed with questions, is that testimony still good enough?
q_conceptual: Why would being asked follow-up questions not undermine the credibility of an offhand remark?

q_practical: Someone says they know my husband died but didn't actually see it happen — is that enough for me to remarry?
q_conceptual: Why does testimony about a death require actually witnessing it, rather than just strong likelihood?

q_practical: My husband fell into the ocean and hasn't been seen since — can I be declared free to remarry?
q_conceptual: Why would falling into open water not count as proof of death, while a sealed body of water would?

q_practical: We saw a body being picked at by a vulture — is that enough to confirm the person is dead?
q_conceptual: Why would where exactly a scavenger is feeding on a body determine whether death can be confirmed?

q_practical: A witness says they saw my husband die in battle but didn't bury him — can I remarry?
q_conceptual: Why would burying the body be the detail that makes someone's testimony about a death trustworthy?

q_practical: There's a war going on and I believe my husband died in it — can I remarry based on that alone?
q_conceptual: Why would a general, plausible cause of death be treated with more suspicion than a specific one?

q_practical: My husband drowned in open water and was never found — can I remarry, and if I already did, do I have to separate?
q_conceptual: Why would permission granted on shaky evidence not be reversed even though it shouldn't have been given?

q_practical: A drowned body washed ashore days later — how do you tell if it's really my husband?
q_conceptual: Why would how long a body has been out of the water affect whether it can still be identified for legal purposes?

q_practical: Someone identified themselves by name before dying, but the body was unrecognizable afterward — can that still count as proof of death?
q_conceptual: Why would a person's own dying statement of identity carry weight even when the body can no longer confirm it?

q_practical: A messenger relayed news of someone's death without knowing who the person was — is that still valid?
q_conceptual: Why would a messenger not needing to know who died still make the report reliable?

q_practical: A foreign traveling companion mentioned my husband died along the way — is that enough for me to remarry?
q_conceptual: Why would someone not knowing the identity of the deceased still not disqualify their testimony?

q_practical: A group of men were led away in chains and a stranger later mentioned they all died — can their wives remarry?
q_conceptual: Why would testimony about a whole group of deaths be accepted the same way as testimony about one person?

q_practical: I heard there was fighting somewhere and believe my husband died there, even though I hadn't heard about the war before — can I remarry?
q_conceptual: Why would not already knowing about a war change how a claim of death in that war is treated?

q_practical: An area had lots of snakes and scorpions and I think my husband was bitten and died — can I remarry on that basis?
q_conceptual: Why would a common, generic cause of death make a claim less believable rather than more?

q_practical: We were trapped in smoke and I escaped but believe my husband didn't — can I remarry?
q_conceptual: Why would your own survival in a dangerous situation cast doubt on your claim that someone else didn't make it?

q_practical: Attackers killed my husband but spared me — is my account enough for me to remarry?
q_conceptual: Why would a woman's survival of an attack that killed her husband be treated as credible rather than suspicious?

q_practical: There's a plague going around and I believe my husband died from it — can I remarry based on that?
q_conceptual: Why would a death during a plague be treated as more believable than one during a war or famine?

q_practical: Some children mentioned details of a man's funeral they'd just come from — can that count as proof of his death?
q_conceptual: Why would children casually describing a funeral's details be accepted as reliable evidence?

q_practical: Can someone who has lost the ability to speak or hear after getting married still divorce their spouse?
q_conceptual: Why would someone's mental competency at the time of an action determine whether that action is legally valid?

q_practical: I had a divorce document prepared before I was even married to her — is it valid once I marry and then divorce her with it?
q_conceptual: Why would a legal document need to be written with a specific future situation already in mind to be valid?

q_practical: Can I appoint someone to act on my behalf in court without them being physically present?
q_conceptual: Why would the law allow open-ended chains of representatives acting for each other?

q_practical: My husband arranged for me to receive divorce papers but died before they reached me — am I considered divorced?
q_conceptual: Why would the timing of a document's delivery relative to someone's death create genuine legal uncertainty?

id: Mishneh Torah, First Fruits and other Gifts to Priests Outside the Sanctuary 2:19
q_practical: How do I formally set aside the first fruit of my field before it's even ripe?
q_conceptual: Why would a verbal declaration on still-unripened produce be enough to lock in its special status?

q_practical: Why would a small amount of a fancy ingredient ruin a whole dish, when a common one wouldn't?
q_conceptual: Why would the value or prestige of a food determine how little of it is needed to make a mixture forbidden?

q_practical: Is it allowed for a free man to have a relationship with a household servant?
q_conceptual: Why would someone in transition between two legal statuses fall into a forbidden category neither status alone would create?

q_practical: Can a convert from a certain background eventually marry into the community, or is that permanently barred?
q_conceptual: Why would a marriage restriction fade out after a couple of generations instead of lasting forever?

q_practical: Why would a group that converted still face a marriage ban even though the law itself doesn't require it?
q_conceptual: Can a leader's decree add a restriction beyond what the underlying law technically demands?

q_practical: Why would a marriage ban on a certain group keep applying even after the reason it was originally tied to no longer exists?
q_conceptual: Can a later ruling detach a restriction from the condition that originally justified it, making it permanent?

q_practical: Why was a marriage ban imposed on a group because of something their ancestors did generations earlier?
q_conceptual: Should a whole group's rights be restricted permanently because of the cruelty of a few of their ancestors?

q_practical: Why does having a child with someone from a forbidden background carry worse consequences than any other forbidden relationship?
q_conceptual: Why would a child's legal status as a member of the community depend on which parent belonged to it?

q_practical: What's the process when a purchased servant undergoes the ritual bath — does he have to be pushed into the water?
q_conceptual: Why would the same ritual bath mean something completely different depending on what the person says while doing it?

q_practical: When a servant is set free, does he need to do the ritual bath all over again?
q_conceptual: Why would a second immersion be needed to complete a conversion that was only partially done the first time?

q_practical: Do converts and freed servants have to follow the same rules for a valid ritual bath as a woman completing her monthly purification?
q_conceptual: Why would completely different life situations share the exact same technical requirements for a valid immersion?

q_practical: If someone converts just to marry a specific person rather than out of genuine belief, is the conversion valid?
q_conceptual: Why would a person's later behavior be used as evidence that their original conversion wasn't sincere?

q_practical: A man claims he converted without his family, but his kids were born before any of them properly converted — does his word count for the kids too?
q_conceptual: Why would someone's own testimony be trusted about themselves but not about other people's status?

q_practical: If someone has lived an observant lifestyle for years but nobody can prove exactly how they converted, can they still marry into the community?
q_conceptual: Why would a lifetime of consistent religious practice not be enough on its own to establish someone's status without formal proof?

q_practical: What's the first thing you ask someone who wants to convert to Judaism?
q_conceptual: Why would prospective converts be warned about hardship up front rather than only told about the benefits?

q_practical: Are there any sexual relationships forbidden to non-Jews the same way certain ones are forbidden to Jews?
q_conceptual: Why would a much shorter list of forbidden relationships apply to people outside a particular religious community?

q_practical: After someone converts, are they still considered related to their birth family for legal purposes?
q_conceptual: Why would conversion be treated as erasing someone's prior family ties entirely?

q_practical: Can a convert marry their own mother or sister if those relatives convert too?
q_conceptual: Why would something technically permitted by the core law still be banned by a later added rule, and for what stated reason?

q_practical: Can a convert marry their father's brother's widow, even though that would be forbidden between two people born Jewish?
q_conceptual: Why would restrictions on marrying relatives apply only through one parent's line and not the other after conversion?

q_practical: Twin brothers who weren't conceived within a recognized marriage but were born into one — does the usual ban on marrying a brother's wife still apply between them?
q_conceptual: Why would the circumstances of birth matter more than the circumstances of conception in defining a family relationship?

q_practical: I married a woman and her daughter, both converts — can I stay married to both, or only one?
q_conceptual: Why would a restriction on marrying two close female relatives end once one of them has died?

q_practical: How much detail about the harder religious obligations do you give someone before they convert?
q_conceptual: Why would you deliberately hold back some of the harsher consequences of a commitment before someone agrees to it?

q_practical: What do you say to a purchased servant instead of asking why they want to convert?
q_conceptual: Why would the question you ask about someone's motives differ depending on whether they're converting freely or as a servant?
